nodes.label: BloomBright.frag
nodes.rationale: First stage of the bloom chain: reads the full-res HDR scene target and writes a quarter-res image containing only the parts bright enough to bloom.

nodes.label: HDR RGBA16F offscreen scene target
nodes.rationale: The scene renders into an unclamped RGBA16F offscreen image so overbright flame/spark values survive to the bloom passes instead of being clipped at 1.0.

nodes.label: Karis soft-knee bright-pass threshold
nodes.rationale: Quadratic ramp through [threshold-knee, threshold+knee] (Karis, SIGGRAPH 2014) instead of a hard cutoff, because a hard cutoff makes the bloom mask flicker as sparks cross the line each frame.

nodes.label: Fused threshold + downsample pass
nodes.rationale: Thresholding and downsampling in one pass halves texture traffic for free, since the four box-filter taps leave nothing for a dedicated downsample pass to do.

nodes.label: Four-tap bilinear box downsample
nodes.rationale: Four half-texel diagonal offsets let bilinear filtering average 2x2 blocks each, covering the full source footprint of a quarter-res output texel for 4 fetches instead of 16.

nodes.label: Karis average (firefly suppression)
nodes.rationale: Each tap is weighted 1/(1+luma) instead of averaged evenly, so a single stray ultra-bright spark pixel can't dominate the mean and make the downsampled quad flicker per-spark.

nodes.label: Quarter-resolution bloom working buffers
nodes.rationale: The bright-pass and both blur passes run at quarter resolution, which is what makes the naive 9-tap blur affordable and is corrected for by bilinear upsampling at composite time.
